## The updater stall is FIXED -- 122 failures and 201 commits of drift ended

Operator approved applying the AC2 patch and running the updater once. Both done. Result:
  updated -> 6125c5345f0117d377acf72975c7c547316e537a
  reject-streak 122 -> 0
  current build cdfd7d94d (2026-08-28) -> 6125c5345f01 (current main)
  prune summary: pruned=2 kept-live=0 remaining=4
Every session on this host now gets gate verdicts from current code, and the on-box MCP server stops
serving five-day-old gate logic. That was a silent correctness risk across all sessions, not just a
staleness annoyance.

Practical note: git apply REFUSES the diff (it names orig.sh/new.sh, being harness-generated); use
patch(1) against the target explicitly. Original backed up to rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak.

The AC-ordering fix paid off immediately and concretely. AC4's proof had originally been 'observe
both findings on this host' -- and AC1 has now DESTROYED that condition, exactly as the plan reviewer
predicted. Because the proof was re-anchored to unit tests against a synthetic state dir with the
live reading demoted to a recorded datum, AC4 is still verifiable. Had it not been re-anchored it
would now be unprovable. Worth remembering: an AC whose evidence a sibling AC eliminates is defective
in the same way a time-dependent AC is.

OPERATOR PRIORITISED 9a17 -- it is blocking other sessions. Change 2600 is now the top item.
Patchset 2 is red on both labels:
 - LLM-Review -1, fair: 'make e2e-deps runs npm ci && npm run build with no failure tolerance, so a
   transient npm/registry failure or offline runner hard-fails the CI Install rebar step.' This is
   the SECOND time this change's CI wiring has risked breaking everyone's builds (the first was the
   unguarded make e2e-deps that test_predates_gate_guard_parity caught). Sent back with the design
   principle rather than a patch instruction: provisioning is an OPTIMISATION and its failure must
   degrade to the in-fixture path, never hard-fail the install step -- the fallback already exists
   because project.portability requires the in-process path to work with no CI provider at all.
 - Verified -1, and NOT the 9a17 signature: scanner-integration failed in 29 SECONDS, far too fast
   for a test run. That workflow (_scanner-integration.yml) arrived recently via change 2595 and may
   be failing independently. Agent told to rebase onto current origin/main BEFORE assuming the
   failure is its own -- a stale base has already produced one misdiagnosis today -- and to report
   back if it turns out to be repo-wide, in which case it is a second blocker to file and escalate
   rather than absorb.
